rv.q: While the new musical MONEY TALKS isn't of Broadway caliber, there's a lot to like about both the book by Tony-nominated Peter Kellogg (Anna KarenINA) and the score by Kellogg and David Friedman.
The Musical, to drop the metaphor, is a seriously disappointing undertaking.
It's not a case of it's so bad it's good. It's just bad.
I couldn't have been more adroitly entertained.
Money Talks has the bones of a really good show, especially with regard to the talented cast.
Money Talks could hit harder, and traffic less in stereotypes we've seen before. But a pleasant summer evening's entertainment? You got it.
This is a pleasant way to spend an afternoon or evening, but don't go into it expecting to have your socks knocked off!
If the characters he encounters had some substance, we might not mind his being paper thin. But they don’t, and we do.
